title: Ašḫella’s ritual

dating.label: attested 14th–13th c. BCE
dating.note: The KUB 9.31 and HT 1 copies used here are dated New Hittite; this is an approximate manuscript date.

purpose: A four-day ritual for plague in an army camp, attributed to Ašḫella of Ḫapalla.
attribution: Attributed to Ašḫella, a man of Ḫapalla

phases.name: Evening
phases.idea: The rams are marked and tethered.

phases.name: Morning
phases.idea: The rams are sent out of camp.

phases.name: Fourth day
phases.idea: Offerings to the Storm-god, Sun-god and all gods.

variants.title: Washing and the two fires
variants.note: The salt-water washing and passage between two fires are explicit in HT 1 + KBo 13.212. KUB 9.31 has broken traces of the fire passage but no clear matching hand-washing section.

steps.title: Prepare a ram
steps.shortDescription: Each army lord supplies a ram at dusk.
steps.summary: Each army lord supplies a ram at dusk.
steps.evidence: Both copies say the colour of the animal does not matter.

image.alt: The ram is shown singly; coat and horn form are illustrative.
image.note: The ram is shown singly; coat and horn form are illustrative.

steps.title: Twist three colours of wool
steps.shortDescription: White, red and green wool are worked into a cord.
steps.summary: White, red and green wool are worked into a cord.
steps.evidence: The translated green term can also be read as yellow-green.

image.alt: A white, red and yellow-green wool cord; exact dye shades and twist are illustrative.
image.note: A white, red and yellow-green wool cord; exact dye shades and twist are illustrative.

steps.title: Bind the cord and rings to the ram
steps.shortDescription: The cord and metal ornaments are fastened to the ram’s neck and horns.
steps.summary: The cord and metal ornaments are fastened to the ram’s neck and horns.
steps.evidence: A mentions iron and lead; B clearly preserves a lead ring. The bead in A is restored.

image.alt: One ram with coloured cord and metal rings; number and placement of ornaments are reconstructed.
image.note: One ram with coloured cord and metal rings; number and placement of ornaments are reconstructed.

steps.title: Tether the ram before a tent
steps.shortDescription: The adorned ram is tied in front of a tent for the night.
steps.summary: The adorned ram is tied in front of a tent for the night.
steps.evidence: The overnight placement is explicit in both copies.

image.alt: A wooden stake and fibre rope stand for the tethering; the exact fixture is not specified.
image.note: A wooden stake and fibre rope stand for the tethering; the exact fixture is not specified.

steps.title: Ask the plague god to be appeased
steps.shortDescription: The speaker asks the god responsible for the plague to accept the tethered rams.
steps.summary: The speaker asks the god responsible for the plague to accept the tethered rams.
steps.evidence: The words address whichever god caused the plague; no named deity is given.

image.alt: The adorned ram is the object named in the address; the speaker’s appearance is unknown.
image.note: The adorned ram is the object named in the address; the speaker’s appearance is unknown.

steps.title: Release the rams at the enemy border
steps.shortDescription: The rams are led through camp and let loose at the enemy border.
steps.summary: The rams are led through camp and let loose at the enemy border.
steps.evidence: The decorated woman, bread and beer also pass through the camp in the text; this unit isolates the rams’ release.

image.alt: A single adorned ram represents the rams released; the route and landscape are not invented.
image.note: A single adorned ram represents the rams released; the route and landscape are not invented.

steps.title: Slaughter a ram on the second day
steps.shortDescription: Six rams are among the animals slaughtered on open ground.
steps.summary: Six rams are among the animals slaughtered on open ground.
steps.patient: One ram from the group of six
steps.evidence: A names six rams and six billy goats in the slaughter batch. B is broken across this part of the second-day procedure.

image.alt: A ram and bronze blade represent one animal in the six-ram group; the exact cutting method is illustrative.
image.note: A ram and bronze blade represent one animal in the six-ram group; the exact cutting method is illustrative.

steps.title: Cook the slaughtered meat
steps.shortDescription: The slaughtered animals are cooked plainly.
steps.summary: The slaughtered animals are cooked plainly.
steps.evidence: The copies specify cooking but not the vessel or technique.

image.alt: A clay cooking vessel and fire illustrate cooking; the vessel and recipe are not prescribed in this passage.
image.note: A clay cooking vessel and fire illustrate cooking; the vessel and recipe are not prescribed in this passage.

steps.title: Wash hands in salted water
steps.shortDescription: Salt is mixed with water, and the participants wash their hands.
steps.summary: Salt is mixed with water, and the participants wash their hands.
steps.evidence: Preserved explicitly in B. A has no corresponding clear hand-washing passage.

image.alt: Hands in a clay bowl of salted water; the bowl is illustrative.
image.note: Hands in a clay bowl of salted water; the bowl is illustrative.

steps.title: Pass between two fires
steps.shortDescription: Two fires are lit, and the participants walk between them.
steps.summary: Two fires are lit, and the participants walk between them.
steps.evidence: B preserves the full instruction. A has broken traces of a fire passage.

image.alt: Two separate wood fires mark the passage; their scale and fuel are illustrative.
image.note: Two separate wood fires mark the passage; their scale and fuel are illustrative.

steps.title: Offer two billy goats
steps.shortDescription: Two billy goats are offered to the Tutelary Deity of the equipment.
steps.summary: Two billy goats are offered to the Tutelary Deity of the equipment.
steps.evidence: The divine epithet and equipment term are difficult to interpret.

image.alt: One goat stands for the pair; its coat and horns are illustrative.
image.note: One goat stands for the pair; its coat and horns are illustrative.

steps.title: Bring a pig on the third day
steps.shortDescription: A pig is driven to a different open place with a goat and ram.
steps.summary: A pig is driven to a different open place with a goat and ram.
steps.evidence: The pig is part of a three-animal group in both copies.

image.alt: A domestic pig cutout; breed and coloration are illustrative.
image.note: A domestic pig cutout; breed and coloration are illustrative.

steps.title: Offer the pig to the plague god
steps.shortDescription: The pig is offered with the goat and ram to the god responsible for the plague.
steps.summary: The pig is offered with the goat and ram to the god responsible for the plague.
steps.evidence: The source groups the three animals in one offering; this unit singles out the pig for comparison.

image.alt: The same pig image marks its offering; the text does not describe the manner of killing here.
image.note: The same pig image marks its offering; the text does not describe the manner of killing here.

steps.title: Offer a bull to the Storm-god
steps.shortDescription: The bull is offered to the Storm-god.
steps.summary: The bull is offered to the Storm-god.
steps.evidence: The fourth-day recipient is explicit in both copies.

image.alt: One bull, full-body cutout; coat and horns are illustrative.
image.note: One bull, full-body cutout; coat and horns are illustrative.

steps.title: Offer a ewe to the Sun-god
steps.shortDescription: A ewe is offered to the Sun-god.
steps.summary: A ewe is offered to the Sun-god.
steps.evidence: The ewe is specified as one that has not been covered by a ram.

image.alt: A single sheep represents the ewe; breed and age are illustrative.
image.note: A single sheep represents the ewe; breed and age are illustrative.

steps.title: Offer three sheep to all the gods
steps.shortDescription: Three sheep are offered to all the gods.
steps.summary: Three sheep are offered to all the gods.
steps.evidence: A says three sheep in the final offering; the illustration shows one animal to keep the unit legible.

image.alt: One sheep represents the group of three; sex is not fixed in both copies.
image.note: One sheep represents the group of three; sex is not fixed in both copies.
